question_scores.question_text: When can I enroll in Medicare and select my coverage? And when can I make changes to my coverage after I've enrolled?
question_scores.response_text:
Enrolling in Medicare is a multi-step process with specific timeframes. There are different "windows" for when you first sign up and when you can make changes later.

Here is a breakdown of the key enrollment periods.

---

### 1. When You First Enroll (Initial Enrollment)

For most people, the first chance to sign up is the **Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)**. This is a 7-month window centered around your 65th birthday:
*   **3 months before** the month you turn 65.
*   **The month** you turn 65.
*   **3 months after** the month you turn 65.

**Note:** If you are already receiving Social Security benefits, you will likely be enrolled in Part A and Part B automatically. If not, you must manually sign up through the Social Security Administration.

#### Special Enrollment Period (SEP)
If you are **still working** and have health coverage through your (or your spouse’s) current employer when you turn 65, you can usually delay Medicare without penalty. You will get an 8-month SEP to sign up for Medicare starting the month after the employment or the insurance coverage ends (whichever happens first).

---

### 2. Selecting Your Coverage
Once you have signed up for **Original Medicare (Part A and Part B)**, you have choices on how to receive your benefits:

*   **Medicare Advantage (Part C):** Private plans that bundle A, B, and usually D (drugs). You can join during your IEP.
*   **Medicare Supplement (Medigap):** Private insurance that pays the "gaps" in Original Medicare. Your best time to buy this is the **6-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period**, which starts the month you are 65 or older AND enrolled in Part B. During this time, companies cannot deny you coverage for pre-existing conditions.
*   **Part D (Prescription Drugs):** You can join a standalone drug plan during your IEP.

---

### 3. When You Can Make Changes (Annual Windows)

After you are enrolled, you aren't locked into your plan forever. There are two main annual windows to make changes:

#### A. Open Enrollment Period (Oct 15 – Dec 7)
This is the most common time to make changes. During this window, you can:
*   Switch from Original Medicare to a Medicare Advantage plan.
*   Switch from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare.
*   Switch from one Medicare Advantage plan to another.
*   Join, drop, or switch a Part D prescription drug plan.
*   *Changes made during this time take effect on **January 1**.*

#### B. Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment (Jan 1 – Mar 31)
If you are **already** in a Medicare Advantage plan, you have a second window to:
*   Switch to a different Medicare Advantage plan.
*   Drop your Medicare Advantage plan and return to Original Medicare (and add a Part D plan).
*   *Note: You cannot use this window to switch from Original Medicare to Medicare Advantage.*

---

### 4. What if I missed my Initial Enrollment?
If you missed your 7-month IEP and don't qualify for a Special Enrollment Period, you must use the **General Enrollment Period**:
*   **When:** January 1 – March 31 each year.
*   **Coverage starts:** The first of the month after you sign up.
*   **Penalty:** You may have to pay a lifetime late-enrollment penalty for Part B and Part D.

### Summary Table
| Period | Dates | Who is it for? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Initial Enrollment (IEP)** | 7-month window around 65th birthday | New retirees/Seniors turning 65 |
| **Open Enrollment** | Oct 15 – Dec 7 | Everyone (Switching plans) |
| **MA Open Enrollment** | Jan 1 – Mar 31 | People already on Medicare Advantage |
| **General Enrollment** | Jan 1 – Mar 31 | People who missed their first chance to sign up |

***Disclaimer:** I am an AI, not a government representative or insurance agent. Medicare rules can be complex. For official guidance, visit [Medicare.gov](https://www.medicare.gov) or call 1-800-MEDICARE.*
